items.title: The Most Important AI News This Week Is Getting Overlooked
items.summary: A week stacked with flashy releases — Muse Wonder and Wonderful, Gemini 4 Argon — and yet the two unassuming Thursday announcements almost nobody is hyping may matter most. Microsoft's MAI Base 2 and Meta's Muse Spark Open won't top the benchmark discourse, but they speak directly to how businesses are actually going to use AI: owning the intelligence layer, tuning their own models, and refusing to hand all their dependencies to one lab.

items.title: Supreme Court appears open to wider video privacy law in Paramount case
items.summary:
The US Supreme Court appeared ready to side with a man who says a Paramount website shared his video history with Facebook. items.title: Microsoft reportedly quits Nscale’s UK data centre weeks before its IPO
items.summary:
Microsoft has pulled out of a deal to anchor Nscale’s first British data centre, the Telegraph reported. The move comes as the AI cloud startup prepares to go public. items.title: Woodside pauses Scarborough gas work after Greenpeace boards platform
items.summary:
Woodside Energy has paused work on its Scarborough gas platform off Western Australia after Greenpeace protesters climbed aboard. Early start-up work at the site has stopped, Australia’s biggest gas exporter said, Bloomberg reported. “Greenpeace’s actions have triggered a significant, potentially costly and entirely avoidable response,” Woodside said. items.title: World Bank backs ‘small AI’ on phones for poorer nations, Guardian reports
items.summary:
The World Bank wants developing countries to build “small AI”, compact models that run on a mobile phone with a weak signal. Paschal Donohoe, the bank’s chief knowledge officer, said AI could speed up growth in emerging economies, but only if it fits local needs, the Guardian reported. items.title: Biotech now sells pet cloning and cryonics, MIT Technology Review finds
items.summary:
